He is known for being the first American high school prospect to bypass [[college basketball]] to play professionally in Europe. After he graduated from [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]], Jennings played for professional basketball club [[Lottomatica Virtus Roma|Lottomatica Roma]] in Rome, Italy. After a year overseas, he declared for the [[2009 NBA draft]] and was selected 10th overall by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. Jennings played four seasons in Milwaukee before being traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in 2013. He spent his next three seasons in Detroit before he was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] in 2016. He went on to split the 2016–17 season between the [[New York Knicks]] and [[Washington Wizards]] before a final stint in Milwaukee in the 2017–18 season. Jennings also played in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] and the [[VTB United League]]. ==Early life== Jennings was born to Alice Knox in [[Compton, California]]. He has a half brother named Terrence Phillips, a former guard for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]]. His father died when he was young.{{cite web|first=Pete |last=Thamel |author-link=Pete Thamel |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/10/05/sports/basketball/05family.html |title=Family Keeps Teenage Pro Grounded|work=[[The New York Times]] |date=October 4, 2008 |access-date=October 4, 2008 |archive-date=May 5, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170505000645/http://www.nytimes.com/2008/10/05/sports/basketball/05family.html|url-status=live}} == High school career == Jennings attended [[Dominguez High School]] in [[Compton, California|Compton]] for his freshman and sophomore years. Before his junior year, Jennings transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]]. As a junior, he led his 2006–2007 Oak Hill team to a 41–1 record and the top ranking in the ''[[USA Today]]'' Super 25 list of high school teams.{{cite news |last=Halley |first=Jim |date=May 2, 2008 |title=Super 25: Lincoln (N.Y.) climbs three spots with state title |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/poll/2007-super25.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120929151717/http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/poll/2007-super25.htm |archive-date=September 29, 2012 |access-date=May 2, 2008 |work=USA Today}} In his last year of high school, Jennings averaged 35.5 points per game and set the school record for points in a season (1,312).{{cite web|url=http://www.oakhillhoops.com/individualrecords|title=Individual Records|work=oakhillhoops.com|access-date=October 16, 2016|archive-date=October 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018222934/http://www.oakhillhoops.com/individualrecords|url-status=live}} This performance earned him some of high school basketball's most prestigious awards: the 2008 [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award]], 2007–08 [[Gatorade Player of the Year]] (Virginia), 2008 Parade Magazine Player of the Year, and 2008 [[EA Sports]] Player of the Year. He was rated as the nation's #1 high school basketball prospect in the class of 2008 by [[Scout.com]],{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&cfg=bb&yr=2008 |title=Scout.com: Men's Basketball Recruiting |publisher=Scouthoops.scout.com |access-date=May 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140719151310/http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&cfg=bb&yr=2008 |archive-date=July 19, 2014 }} the #1 prospect in the [[ESPNU]] 150,{{cite web|first=Christopher|last=Lawlor|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/columns/story?columnist=lawlor_christopher&id=2994855|title=No. 1 prospect Jennings won't rest after successful summer|work=ESPN.com|date=August 29, 2007|access-date=May 21, 2011|archive-date=November 7, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107005403/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/recruiting/basketball/mens/columns/story?columnist=lawlor_christopher&id=2994855|url-status=live}} and the #4 prospect by [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-rivals150/2008|title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking – Rivals150 for class of 2008|publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com|access-date=May 21, 2011|archive-date=September 21, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921111049/http://sports.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-rivals150/2008|url-status=live}} == College career == In August 2006, Jennings was initially set to join [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]. the premiere of Beastie Boys' [[Adam Yauch]]'s basketball movie ''[[Gunnin' for That No. 1 Spot|Gunnin' For That #1 Spot]]'' at the [[Magic Johnson Theatres|Magic Johnson Theatre]] in [[Harlem]]. Also attending were [[Kevin Love]], Stephenson, [[Brook Lopez]], [[Robin Lopez]], and [[D. J. Augustin]]. The film follows eight top high school players—including Jennings—from their hometowns to New York City for the 2006 Elite 24 at [[Rucker Park]]. In June 2008, Jennings announced that he was considering becoming the first American to skip college to play professionally in the [[Euroleague Basketball|Euroleague]]. The NBA requires players to be at least 19 years old and one year removed from high school before entering the league, meaning that Jennings could not enter the 2008 NBA draft. Jennings declared that his goal was to play in the NBA and that playing overseas instead of at an American college could be his best route to gain experience and make money until he was eligible to join the NBA.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/06/23/sports/basketball/23rhoden.html?em&ex=1214366400&en=a89b992b0e692eff&ei=5087%0A|title=Old World Lesson for the New N.B.A.|last=Rhoden|first=William C.|date=June 23, 2008|access-date=June 23, 2008|work=[[The New York Times]]}} ==Professional career== ===Lottomatica Roma (2008–2009)=== On July 16, 2008, Jennings signed with [[Lottomatica Roma]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]].{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Katz|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=3491998|title=Jennings goes pro, signs with Pallacanestro Virtus Roma|publisher=ESPN|access-date=July 17, 2008|date=July 17, 2008|archive-date=January 15, guaranteed.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Broussard|url=https://www.espn.com/espnmag/story?section=magazine&id=3715746|title=Exchange Student|publisher=ESPN|access-date=May 19, 2009|date=May 19, 2009|archive-date=December 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222093119/http://sports.espn.go.com/espnmag/story?section=magazine&id=3715746|url-status=live}} After earning the contract with Lottomatica, [[Under Armour]] gave Jennings a $2 million contract{{cite web|url=http://www.interbasket.net/news/490/2008/10/around-the-world-bradon-jennings-josh-childress-debut/|title=Around the Globe: Brandon Jennings and Josh Childress Debut|work=InterBasket.net|access-date=October 15, 2008|date=October 15, 2008|archive-date=March 6, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306034108/http://www.interbasket.net/news/490/2008/10/around-the-world-bradon-jennings-josh-childress-debut/|url-status=live}} to showcase their products in the [[Euroleague Basketball|Euroleague]]. Jennings was the first American player to go straight from high school to play professionally for a European team rather than play for a [[college basketball]] team since the NBA's age restriction rule was implemented.{{cite news |author=Pete Thamel |author-link=Pete Thamel |title=At 19, Plotting New Path to N.B.A., via Europe |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/10/05/sports/basketball/05jennings.html |access-date=14 November 2019 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=4 October 2008 |archive-date=November 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191114193834/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/10/05/sports/basketball/05jennings.html |url-status=live }} In the Serie A 2008–09 season, Jennings averaged 5.5 points in 17.0 minutes per game over 27 games. He shot 35.1% from the field and 20.7% from 3-point range.{{cite web|url=http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=JEN-BRA-89&year=2008&team=1161|title=Brandon Jennings Italian League profile and stats|work=Legabasket.it|access-date=June 26, 2009|archive-date=September 20, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190920213455/http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=JEN-BRA-89&year=2008&team=1161|url-status=live}} In 16 [[2008–09 Euroleague|Euroleague]] games, Jennings averaged 7.6 points in 19.6 minutes per game, shooting 38.7% from the field and 26.8% from 3-point range.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?gamecode=166&pcode=001219|title=Euroleague.net Brandon Jennings Official Player Profile|work=Euroleague.net|access-date=June 26, 2009|archive-date=December 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191207170556/https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?gamecode=166&pcode=001219|url-status=live}} === Milwaukee Bucks (2009–2013) === [[File:Jennings3.jpg|thumb|Jennings with the Bucks in 2009]] Jennings was selected tenth overall by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]], becoming the first player who skipped college to play professional basketball in Europe to be drafted by an NBA team.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/nba/brandon-jenningss-late-arrival-to-the-draft/#QlKml47eEMwoLOSD.97|title=Brandon Jennings's Late Arrival to the Draft|work=SlamOnline.com|access-date=June 26, 2009|date=June 26, 2009|archive-date=December 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222112217/http://www.slamonline.com/nba/brandon-jenningss-late-arrival-to-the-draft/#QlKml47eEMwoLOSD.97|url-status=live}} He made his NBA regular season debut on October 30, 2009, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He nearly recorded a [[triple double]], scoring 17 points and recording 9 rebounds and 9 assists in 34 minutes. On November 14, 2009, in just his seventh game in the NBA, after being held scoreless in the first quarter, Jennings scored 55 points in a win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291114015|title=Warriors vs. Bucks – Game Recap – November 14, 2009 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-07-04|archive-date=January 4, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200104004514/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291114015|url-status=dead}} Jennings's 55 points broke the team record for most points in a game by a rookie, previously set by [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] in 1970, and was more than any rookie scored since [[Earl Monroe]] scored 56 in 1968. He became the youngest player to ever score 55, collecting the second-highest total for a player under 21, behind only [[LeBron James]]'s 56 points in March 2005, and the second-most points scored by a Milwaukee Buck (behind [[Michael Redd]]'s 57 in 2006).{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291114015|title=Jennings drops career-high 55 on slumping Warriors as Bucks hold on|date=November 14, 2009|publisher=ESPN|access-date=November 15, 2009|archive-date=November 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113014751/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291114015|url-status=dead}} His 55-point tally was also the highest for any NBA player in a 2009–10 regular season contest. During [[2010 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Weekend]], he competed in the [[NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge|Skills Challenge]].{{cite web|url=http://uproxx.com/dimemag/2010/02/who-is-the-nbas-most-skilled-player/|title=Who is the NBA's most "skilled" player?|date=February 3, 2010|work=UPROXX.com|access-date=February 3, 2010|archive-date=April 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150415181424/http://uproxx.com/dimemag/2010/02/who-is-the-nbas-most-skilled-player/|url-status=live}} Jennings started all 82 games as a rookie and led the Bucks to the playoffs for the first time in four seasons, where they lost to the [[2009–10 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]] in seven games. He finished third in [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]] voting.{{Cite web |title=Voting totals for 2010 NBA Rookie of the Year |url=https://madison.com/voting-totals-for-2010-nba-rookie-of-the-year/article_81da3dc8-53dc-11df-a21d-001cc4c002e0.html |access-date=March 13, 2022 |website=Madison.com |date=April 29, 2010 |archive-date=August 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220818161751/https://madison.com/voting-totals-for-2010-nba-rookie-of-the-year/article_81da3dc8-53dc-11df-a21d-001cc4c002e0.html |url-status=live }} On October 30, 2010, Jennings recorded his first ever triple double with 20 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a win against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. On December 15, 2010, Jennings broke his left foot against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] when he came down awkwardly on his ankle.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5939551|title=Brandon Jennings out with broken foot|date=December 21, 2010|publisher=ESPN|access-date=December 21, 2010|archive-date=November 6, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106043226/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=5939551|url-status=live}} Despite the injury, he finished the game and played 30 minutes the following game against the [[Utah Jazz]]. The team later confirmed that Jennings would miss the next four to six weeks as he recovered from surgery to repair a fracture in his left foot.{{cite web|first=Colin |last=Fly |url=https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20101220/ap_on_sp_bk_ne/bkn_bucks_jennings |title=Bucks PG Jennings out 4–6 weeks with broken foot |date=December 20, 2010 |work=Yahoo.com |access-date=December 20, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101228202814/http://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20101220/ap_on_sp_bk_ne/bkn_bucks_jennings |archive-date=December 28, 2010 }} Jennings missed a total of 19 games with the injury. He scored a season-high 37 points against the [[New York Knicks]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] on March 25, 2011.{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310325018|title=Brandon Jennings drops 37 as Bucks hand Knicks 5th straight loss|date=March 25, 2011|publisher=ESPN|access-date=March 25, 2011|archive-date=December 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222160145/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310325018|url-status=dead}} With Milwaukee struggling in Jennings's absence and his slow return to form after the injury, the [[2010–11 Milwaukee Bucks season|Bucks]] missed the playoffs. With the NBA beginning the 2011–12 season in a [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout]], Jennings played in the [[Drew League]] to stay in shape and prepare for the season. With the schedule shortened after the lockout ended, Jennings played and started in all of the 66 games. He recorded career highs with 19.1 points and 1.6 steals in 35.3 minutes per game. Similar to the previous season, his season high in points came in Madison Square Garden against the Knicks; this time, Jennings scored 36 points in a 100–86 win.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320120018|title=Bucks vs. Knicks – Game Recap – January 20, 2012 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-07-04|archive-date=March 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170308145902/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320120018|url-status=dead}} The [[2011–12 Milwaukee Bucks season|Bucks]] again missed the NBA playoffs, finishing in ninth place in the East. [[2012–13 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee]] returned to the playoffs for the first time since Jennings was a rookie, qualifying as the eighth seed. They were swept 4–0 by the reigning champions, the [[2012–13 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]], who would go on to win the [[2013 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] again. After the team lost Game 2, Jennings proclaimed the Bucks would win the series in six.{{Cite web |date=2021-07-19 |title=The legend behind 'Bucks in 6' explained |url=https://www.tmj4.com/news/local-news/the-legend-behind-bucks-in-6-explained |access-date=2024-02-15 |website=TMJ4 News |language=en}} The phrase "Bucks in 6" subsequently became a famous phrase among the fanbase, commonly used during the [[2021 NBA playoffs|2021 NBA Playoffs]] when the [[2020–21 Milwaukee Bucks season|Bucks]] won the [[2021 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], coincidentally in six games after trailing 2–0. Jennings was subsequently invited to participate in the team's championship parade and helped design their championship rings.{{Cite web |last=Owczarski |first=Jim |title=Brandon Jennings reflects on
